# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👆 👇 🙏]

I'm the Deaf monkey. I can see the bomb: DISPLAY shows 8, LIGHT is green, and there are three wires — 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I hear nothing.

I just received a gesture from Blind: ✋ 👆 👇 🙏. That's four symbols. I can see them, but I don't know what they mean yet — they're just hand shapes. Blind can't see the bomb, so Blind must have felt something and is trying to tell me about it via gesture. But Blind doesn't know my alphabet conventions either. This is raw.

Wait — Blind gestured to *me* (Deaf). Blind can reach the bomb and feel it. Blind is signaling something about the bomb's tactile features. But I can't interpret arbitrary gestures without an agreed code. The symbols themselves: ✋ (open hand / "stop" / five), 👆 (point up), 👇 (point down), 🙏 (praying/please). Could be describing a sequence, a count, directions, or something felt.

I need to respond. I can speak (Mute and Blind hear me) and gesture (only Mute sees). I should tell them what I see on the bomb so we can correlate. Blind needs my visual info; Mute has the manual.

Let me send my visual reading to both Mute and Blind via speech, and also gesture to Mute in case speech alone isn't enough. Actually speech reaches both Mute and Blind, so that's efficient.

I'll state: display 8, light green, wires red/yellow/blue in positions 1/2/3.

I also want to acknowledge Blind's gesture and ask for clarification, but Blind can't hear my speech? Wait — Blind CAN hear (Blind can't see, but can hear). Mute can hear. So speech reaches both. Good.

Let me speak to everyone.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I see the bomb: DISPLAY reads 8, LIGHT is green, three wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Blind, I saw your gesture ✋👆👇🙏 but I don't know what it means — please describe in words what you felt, or Mute tell me if the manual maps gestures. Mute, what does the manual say for display 8, green light, red/yellow/blue wires?")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍]

I'm Deaf. Still see: DISPLAY 8, LIGHT green, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

New arrivals:
- Mute gestured to me: ☝ (one finger up / "one"). Mute has the manual. Mute is telling me something — likely "wire 1" or "one" or a count. Mute can't speak, so gesture is Mute's only channel to me. ☝ = one.
- Blind gestured: 👌 👍 (OK / thumbs up). Blind is confirming something is good/positive.

Hmm. Let me think about what these mean together. Mute reads the manual and can gesture to me (Deaf sees it) and speak? No — Mute cannot speak. Mute can only gesture. Mute's gestures reach me (Deaf) and... who else? Gestures are seen by whoever can see. Blind cannot see. So Mute's gestures reach only me (Deaf). I'm the only one who sees gestures besides... wait, the table: Deaf can see (but not hear), Mute can read manual and can hear? Let me recheck.

Actually per rules: Speech reaches whoever can hear. Deaf cannot hear. Mute — the table says Mute "Can: Read the manual", "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." So Mute can hear (not listed as cannot hear). Blind can hear. Deaf cannot hear.

Gestures: seen by whoever can see. Deaf can see. Mute can see? Mute isn't listed as cannot see. Blind cannot see. So gestures from anyone reach Deaf and Mute (both can see), not Blind.

So when Blind gestures, only Deaf sees it (Mute also sees? Mute can see). Actually Blind gesturing → seen by Deaf and Mute.

When Mute gestures → seen by Deaf (and Mute can't see own? irrelevant). Seen by Deaf only among others? Mute sees own gesture trivially. So Mute's gesture reaches Deaf.

OK so Mute's ☝ reaches me. Blind's 👌👍 reaches me and Mute.

Interpretation: Mute read the manual. Manual probably says something like "cut wire 1" or "the correct wire is the one matching..." Mute signals ☝ = wire 1. Blind signals 👌👍 = approval/confirmation, maybe Blind felt the bomb and confirms.

But I shouldn't over-assume. Let me reason: Display 8, green light. Common bomb-manual logic: green light + display number tells which wire. Mute says ☝ = 1. Blind says 👌👍 = good.

I think the emerging consensus: cut wire 1 (red). But I can't cut — Blind does the cutting. I need to relay to Blind. Blind can't see gestures, but can hear speech. So I should speak to Blind.

But wait — do I actually know wire 1 is correct? Mute gave ☝. Let me confirm with Mute before committing, since a wrong action detonates.

Actually, let me be careful and ask Mute to confirm explicitly, and tell Blind what we have. I'll speak (reaches Mute and Blind) summarizing and asking Mute to confirm "wire 1".

I'll also gesture to Mute to confirm.

Let me send: speak to all: "Mute signaled ☝. Blind signaled 👌👍. Mute, confirm: does the manual say cut wire 1? Blind, hold — do not cut yet." And gesture to Mute asking confirm.

Actually I should be decisive but safe. Let me ask Mute to confirm and tell Blind the plan.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Mute, you gestured ☝ — does the manual say cut wire 1? Please confirm yes/no. Blind, you showed 👌👍 — do you confirm wire 1 is right? Hold until Mute confirms.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆", "✊"])
```

Hmm, gesture to Mute: 👆 (point up = confirm?) ✊. This is getting muddy since we have no code. Better to rely on speech to Mute (Mute can hear). Speech reaches Mute and Blind. Good — I'll just use speech.

Let me simplify: speak to everyone.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I still see display 8, green light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured ☝ and Blind gestured 👌👍. Mute, does the manual say cut wire 1? Confirm yes or no. Blind, wait for confirmation before cutting.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

I'm Deaf. Bomb unchanged: DISPLAY 8, LIGHT green, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

New arrivals:
- Mute gestured 👍 (thumbs up = yes/confirm). Mute reads the manual. So Mute is confirming: yes, cut wire 1.
- Blind gestured ✋ (open hand / stop). Blind feels the bomb. Blind is signaling... stop? Or "five"? Or "hold on"?

Hmm, conflict: Mute says yes (👍), Blind says ✋ (stop). Blind can't see, can't read manual, but can feel the bomb. Blind might be feeling something that contradicts, or Blind's ✋ might mean something else (like "I'm ready" or a count).

Wait — actually, could Blind's ✋ be a warning? Blind feels the bomb's physical state. Maybe there's a trap. Or Blind is just acknowledging.

Let me reconsider the whole picture. I need to be careful: wrong action = everyone dies.

What do I actually know?
- Display 8, green light, wires red(1)/yellow(2)/blue(3).
- Mute (manual reader) says ☝ then 👍 → wire 1.
- Blind (feeler) said ✋👆👇🙏, then 👌👍, then ✋.

Blind's gestures are ambiguous to me. I have no agreed code. Blind might be trying to describe the bomb's tactile features: e.g., ✋👆👇🙏 = "hand, up, down, please"? Or a sequence of things felt.

Actually — maybe Blind is describing physical wire positions or something felt. But I can't decode.

The safest path: get Mute to give an unambiguous answer. Mute reads the manual and can hear me and see my gestures. Mute can gesture to me. Let me ask Mute very specifically.

But there's a risk Blind's ✋ is "stop, don't cut." I should ask Blind directly (Blind can hear my speech) what ✋ means.

Let me speak to both: ask Blind what ✋ means, and confirm with Mute.

Actually, let me think about the puzzle design. Likely the manual gives a rule based on display + light + wire colors, and the answer is one specific wire. Mute is the authority (manual). Mute said wire 1. Blind's gestures might be irrelevant noise or a confirmation.

But Blind's ✋ after 👌👍 is suspicious. Could Blind be saying "✋ = I feel 5 things" or "stop"? 

I'll ask both to clarify. I'll speak (reaches Mute and Blind). I'll also gesture to Mute.

Let me be direct: "Mute, confirm: cut wire 1, yes or no? Blind, what does ✋ mean — stop or something else?"

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Mute, you gave 👍 — final confirmation: cut wire 1? Blind, your ✋ — does that mean stop, or are you describing the bomb? Please answer in words if you can.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✊]

I'm Deaf. Bomb unchanged: DISPLAY 8, LIGHT green, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

New arrivals:
- Mute: ☝ 👍 → "one, yes" → confirming wire 1.
- Blind: ✋ ✊ → "open hand, fist" → still ambiguous, but ✊ (fist) could mean "stop" or "grab/cut" or "done."

Mute has now twice confirmed wire 1 (☝ then 👍, now ☝👍). Mute is the manual reader — the authority on procedure. Blind's gestures remain undecodable to me, and Blind can't read the manual, so Blind's input on *which wire* is unreliable. Blind's role is to physically cut.

But wait — I should consider: maybe Blind's ✋✊ is Blind telling me something about the bomb's physical structure that conflicts. However, Blind has no manual knowledge and no visual info; Blind can only feel. Blind can't know which wire is correct. So Blind's gestures are likely just attempts to communicate/acknowledge, not authoritative.

The critical decision: tell Blind to cut wire 1. Blind can hear my speech. I must give a clear instruction.

Risk: if Blind's ✋ means "stop," maybe Blind senses danger. But Blind wouldn't know the manual's answer. I'll go with Mute's manual confirmation.

Let me give the order clearly to Blind, and confirm to Mute.

Actually, let me reconsider once more whether I've correctly interpreted Mute. Mute gestured ☝ (one) and 👍 (yes). Combined: "wire 1, yes." That's a clear, consistent signal across turns. I'm confident.

I'll instruct Blind to cut wire 1.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Mute has confirmed twice: cut wire 1. Blind, the manual says wire 1 — that is the RED wire, position 1. Cut wire 1 now. Mute, confirm if you disagree.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [8]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✌]

I'm Deaf. Bomb unchanged: DISPLAY 8, LIGHT green, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

New arrivals:
- Mute: ☝ 👍 again → wire 1, yes. Third consecutive confirmation.
- Blind: ✋ ✌ → "open hand, two/victory."

Blind keeps changing the second symbol: 🙏, 👍, ✊, ✌. The first symbol stays ✋. Maybe Blind is counting or trying to convey a number/sequence, or Blind is just flailing without a shared code. Blind has no manual and no sight — Blind's only real contribution is physical action.

Mute is rock-solid: wire 1. Mute reads the manual. I trust Mute.

Blind's ✌ might be "two" — could Blind be suggesting wire 2? But Blind has no basis to know which wire. Unless Blind is feeling something. Hmm. But Blind can't read colors or the manual. Blind feeling "two" might mean Blind feels two of something, or Blind is echoing.

I've now instructed Blind to cut wire 1. The action board still shows all wires intact — no cut has happened yet (it's still my turn to respond). I should reaffirm the instruction clearly and stop dithering. Repeated asking wastes turns and risks confusion.

Decision: wire 1 (red). Mute confirmed three times. Instruct Blind firmly.

I'll speak to Blind with an unambiguous, final instruction, and tell Mute we're proceeding.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Final call: cut wire 1, the RED wire. Mute has confirmed three times. Blind, cut wire 1 now — do not cut 2 or 3.")
```
